newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon complains of bus attack, Israel denies it.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon complains of bus attack, Israel denies it.

text.p: Lebanon complained on Monday that Israeli troops violated a ceasefire by shooting at a school bus carrying 30 students, official sources said.
The Lebanese official sources said Israeli gunfire sprayed the bus on the road to Qilya in the southern tip of the Bekaa Valley on Sunday.
"The school bus was hit by many bullets but the children escaped a massacre...This is a clear violation to the ceasefire understanding," one source said.
In Israel, an army spokesman said: "The Israeli army denies all the reports by foreign press that Israeli forces fired at a bus that was carrying Lebanese civilians."
The Lebanese sources said the five-nation group monitoring the truce would discuss the complaint on Tuesday. The committee comprises the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel.

The committee would also discuss an Israeli complaint filed against Lebanon two days earlier after an Israeli soldier was wounded by mortar bombs fired by Moslem guerrillas on a border outpost, the sources added.
A U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding on April 26 last year ended a 17-day Israeli blitz against pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas in Lebanon.
The ceasefire agreement does not bar guerrilla raids on Israeli forces occupying a 15-km (nine-mile) wide border zone in south Lebanon and gives both sides the right to self-defence.
